name: nightlight
description: Nightlight is a self-hosted baby monitor with low-latency multi-camera streaming from RTSP cameras, installable as a web app (PWA) on your phone. No cloud, no subscription - runs entirely on your own network. One container includes the app, MediaMTX (RTSP to WebRTC/HLS bridge), and FFmpeg (audio transcoding) together. Nightlight needs a routable LAN address so WebRTC (the low-latency viewing mode) works correctly. Host networking (the default below) is the simplest way to get one and needs no extra setup; a dedicated ipvlan/macvlan address on a custom Docker network is also supported if you'd rather avoid host-mode port conflicts - see the Networking modes section of the README (github.com/sauso/nightlight) for both options. Set the data path below to somewhere under your appdata share before starting. After starting, open the WebUI and you'll be prompted to create the first admin account.

paths.name: Data Directory
paths.description: Stores the database and MediaMTX's config (including your added cameras)

paths.name: Recordings Directory (optional)
paths.description: OPTIONAL - where event-recording clips are stored. Leave unset and clips go under the Data Directory (your SSD cache). To keep large clips off the SSD, map this to a folder on your array (e.g. /mnt/user/nightlight-clips) AND set the CLIPS_DIR variable below to /recordings. Retention caps (Settings - Recording) protect the disk either way.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: Used ONLY to build the WebUI link above - with Host networking (the default), changing this number does NOT change the port the app actually listens on. To actually change the port, set the PORT variable below to the SAME number as this field.

variables.name: PORT
variables.description: OPTIONAL - the port the app actually listens on. Leave blank for the default (4000). If you set this, also change WebUI Port above to the same number, or the WebUI link will point at the wrong port.

variables.name: CLIPS_DIR
variables.description: OPTIONAL - set to /recordings only if you mapped the Recordings Directory above to store clips on your array instead of under the Data Directory. Leave blank otherwise.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User ID that owns files this container creates in the Data Directory - 99 matches Unraid's own 'nobody' convention, so the default should already be correct

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group ID that owns files this container creates in the Data Directory - 100 matches Unraid's own 'users' convention, so the default should already be correct

variables.name: Timezone
variables.description: Your local timezone, e.g. Australia/Melbourne - affects log timestamps only

variables.name: JWT Secret
variables.description: Optional - leave blank and a secure random secret is generated and persisted in the data directory automatically on first run

variables.name: Public Host
variables.description: Your public IP or DDNS hostname - only needed if you want Low Latency (WebRTC) mode to work from outside your home network (also requires forwarding UDP port 8189 on your router). Leave blank for LAN-only use.
